All wells, documents and events here are synthetic (synthetic_assam). The numbers measure the method on data built around its own physics; they are an upper bound, not field performance.

Method

Leave-one-well-out: for each held-out well, analogues and the hazard roadmap are built from the other wells only (basin rates exclude the held-out well), the well's real-time data is generated from its survey, casing and DDR-recorded events, served by the WITSML simulator, read by the WITSML poller and processed by the live service (store, rig state, derived channels, detectors, fusion, alarm policy). Depth windows around each recorded event are replayed (120 m above to 40 m below). An event is detected when an alert of its hazard is raised from 6 h before its recorded start until 30 min after it ends; lead time is the recorded start minus the first such alert (negative: detected after the start). False alerts match no event; rate per 24 operating hours. Brier: mean squared error of the posterior against "inside an event" over every 5-second evaluation.
